name: leak-stat
hook: Ninety-eight out of a hundred people hit your site and just leave.

name: leak-confession
hook: I spent four grand on clicks last month. Two of them called me.

name: leak-contrarian
hook: Your website isn't broken. It's leaking exactly the way they designed it.

name: race-stat
hook: Every shared lead I buy goes to four other guys the same second.

name: race-confession
hook: I lost a job to a guy who got my lead before I finished reading it.

name: race-contrarian
hook: A shared lead isn't a lead. It's a footrace you paid to enter.

name: ftc-stat
hook: The biggest lead site got fined seven point two million for lying about lead quality.

name: ftc-confession
hook: Turns out my garbage leads weren't my fault. There's a paper trail.

name: ftc-contrarian
hook: If your leads feel like junk, they might literally be junk.

name: robot-stat
hook: A robot charged me four hundred bucks because my own customer called me back.

name: robot-confession
hook: I got billed for a lead that was already my customer. Couldn't even argue.

name: robot-contrarian
hook: Your own website traffic never bills you by algorithm.

name: ghost-stat
hook: Thirty leads last month. Thirty ghosts. Paid for every one.

name: ghost-confession
hook: I called the same dead number six times before I gave up.

name: ghost-contrarian
hook: The people already on your site want the work. The bought ones don't.

name: math-stat
hook: A hundred bucks for a shared lead I close maybe five percent of the time.

name: math-confession
hook: I did the math on my lead spend and almost parked the truck.

name: math-contrarian
hook: Seven dollars for a lead that's mine, or a hundred for one that's everyone's.

name: credit-stat
hook: They don't refund bad leads. They give you credit to buy more bad leads.

name: credit-confession
hook: I disputed a fake lead and they credited me — to spend with them again.

name: credit-contrarian
hook: A refund gives your money back. A credit just keeps you on the hook.

name: creepy-stat
hook: I tried a visitor-ID tool once. First week, someone asked why they were on a list.

name: creepy-confession
hook: Someone replied 'why am I on this list,' and I never opened it again.

name: creepy-contrarian
hook: Consent-first means the person actually expects to hear from you.

name: twice-stat
hook: They sold me the same homeowner twice. Second time, the job was already done.

name: twice-confession
hook: I paid for a lead I'd already lost — same name, two weeks later.

name: twice-contrarian
hook: Exclusive used to mean something. With us it still does — sold once, to you.

name: ownership-stat
hook: Every dollar I gave the lead sites built their brand, not mine.

name: ownership-confession
hook: I built someone else's pipeline for three years before I noticed.

name: ownership-contrarian
hook: You don't own a lead you rent. Your website is the one pipe that's yours.

name: nonugc-leak-stat
hook: 98 of 100 visitors leave your site.

name: nonugc-leak-confession
hook: You paid for every click — and most you never see again.

name: nonugc-leak-contrarian
hook: The leak isn't a bug. It's the business model.

name: nonugc-math-stat
hook: $575 to land one job on shared leads.

name: nonugc-math-confession
hook: Add up your lead spend per booked job. Maybe sit down first.

name: nonugc-math-contrarian
hook: Same job — $575 the old way, $140 the new way.

name: nonugc-ftc-stat
hook: $7.2M fine for lying about lead quality.

name: nonugc-ftc-confession
hook: Your bad leads, finally explained.

name: nonugc-ftc-contrarian
hook: It isn't bad luck. It's documented.

name: nonugc-ownership-stat
hook: One pipe you actually own: your website.

name: nonugc-ownership-confession
hook: Rent your leads and one policy change can end you.

name: nonugc-ownership-contrarian
hook: Stop building their brand with your ad budget.
